articles.title_orig: A fire devastates the Eagle’s Nest retreat built for Hitler in Germany. A suspect is detained
articles.title_zh: A fire devastates the Eagle’s Nest retreat built for Hitler in Germany. A suspect is detained
articles.content_orig:
About 200 firefighters deployed to tackle blaze at former Nazi mountain retreat in remote part of southern Germany
Police have arrested a 33-year-old German citizen after a fire ripped through Adolf Hitler’s former mountain retreat in Bavaria, leaving the historic Nazi meeting place – known as the Eagle’s Nest – largely destroyed.
About 200 firefighters were deployed on Friday night to tackle the blaze at the Nazi dictator’s remote, purpose-built Kehlsteinhaus residence, a protected building on the peak of Obersalzberg in southern Germany .
Flames rose high into the air as firefighters approached the scene to find the building “completely ablaze”, police said, adding that nobody was injured in the fire.
Lisa Maier, a police spokesperson, said firefighters struggled to tackle the blaze due to its location at an altitude of 1,834 metres (6,000ft).
The building, which was one of the few undamaged monuments of the Hitler era, was only accessible with “heavy breathing apparatus”, she said.
Built by the Nazis and formally inaugurated by Hitler on his birthday in 1939, the Eagle’s Nest has been preserved as a monument to “the insanity of the regime”, according to its website .
The building is only accessible via a road cut into the mountain through previously impassable terrain. Nazis would enter a tunnel and take a 124-metre brass lift buried in the mountain to get inside the building.
Authorities were alerted to the fire when a smoke detector triggered a fire alarm at about 9.15pm, police said. When firefighters arrived on the scene at about 9.50pm, the entire building was engulfed in flames.
Fire departments from six municipalities sent emergency personnel to tackle the blaze and the Bavarian Red Cross, the local mountain rescue service and the police also attended.
No reason for the fire was given, but German media reported that investigators suspected it was the result of arson. Firefighters found no one inside the building.
Efforts to fight the fire were hampered by a strong wind and rain, which turned into the year’s first snow, and firefighters had to pull out overnight after several hours.
The blaze was reportedly still burning at 7am on Saturday but appeared to be out later in the morning, although smoke continued to rise from the building.
A police spokesperson told the German tabloid Bild: “It is damaged to a large extent. The house is unlikely to be saved.” Officers blocked access to the road leading to the retreat, according to an Agence France-Presse photographer.
Maier said police were still investigating and would hold a news conference later on Saturday.
after newsletter promotion
The 33-year-old suspect arrested by the police was a German citizen who had ties to the area but did not live there. Prosecutors said he showed signs of mental illness and after being questioned he was being sent to a psychiatric facility.
The possibility of a political motive for the blaze would be investigated, but police said there was nothing to indicate anyone else was involved.
The Eagle’s Nest was constructed between 1937 and 1938 and forms part of the toxic legacy of Hitler’s Third Reich, which was responsible for the deaths of millions of Jews as well as Roma, LGBTQ people and communists in the Holocaust .
It became legendary in the postwar period and was often depicted as an essential meeting place in US war films, although in reality Hitler rarely visited the complex.
Since 1952 the building has housed an exhibition by the Institute for Contemporary History recounting its Nazi history, and a restaurant.
Officials indicated that the building, which is owned by Bavaria’s state government, would be restored after discussions with local officials, historians and conservators.
“We’re not going to leave a ruin there,” Joachim Herrmann, Bavaria’s interior minister, told reporters, adding that it was important to continue to do “the work of remembrance”.
Agence France-Presse contributed to this report

articles.title_zh: Violence flares in Paris after largely peaceful protests across France
articles.content_orig:

The Louvre is closed on Saturday, along with several other major Paris museums, because of concerns about potential violence during planned protests , France 's culture ministry says.
The Orsay and Picasso museums are also among those that are closed, the ministry said.
The ministry called on all institutions under its authority to adopt any necessary measures to ensure “visitor safety, staff protection and the preservation of artworks”.
The closures follow protests last Saturday that descended into mayhem, with rioters setting fires, smashing shop windows, looting and clashing with police.
The clashes and widespread looting over the weekend marked France's most violent unrest in years, and the French capital has been gripped by social tension.
Art Basel Paris is among those taking the same tack.
After two days when admission was invite-only, the fair opened to the public on Friday – but only for the day.
Organisers cancelled the weekend program on Thursday, prompted by the threat of unrest.
The fair's Paris venue, the Grand Palais, is hosting 211 international galleries and their exhibitions for Art Basel, considered one of the world's most prestigious contemporary art fairs.
“It’s kind of like the art Olympics,” New York-based artist Drake Carr, who is showing his work with Mariposa Gallery, said.
A protest on Thursday afternoon in Paris was peaceful, and Art Basel's organisers announced the decision to close for the weekend around the same time.
The protest planned for Saturday is expected to be much larger.
"This decision has not been taken lightly, and the safety of everyone involved in the fair remains our utmost priority," organizers said in a statement.
Its website posted a similar announcement and said that weekend ticketholders would be contacted.
Saloni Doshi, an art collector who travelled to Paris from India for the fair, grew worried last Saturday as she saw the fires and panicked people.
She received phone calls from friends asking whether Paris was safe.
She agreed with the organisers' rationale to close.
“It's hard that something like this has to happen, but state activities and people's freedom have to continue,” she said.
“I cannot imagine that a bunch of elite, privileged people getting inconvenienced because of this should have a voice.”
Antoine Donzeaud and Elisa Rigoulet, the owners of the gallery exo exo, felt the same.
“We understand this decision, which we consider reasonable and consistent with the urgency of the social demands currently unfolding in France,” they said in a text message.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine’s Starlink speeds restored after week of frontline disruption
articles.title_zh: Ukraine’s Starlink speeds restored after week of frontline disruption
articles.content_orig:
Questions persist about who ordered the interruptions to the satellite internet system that Kyiv’s forces rely on to counter Russian attacks
Ukraine’s access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to the speeds it had before restrictions that disrupted frontline operations for more than a week, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday.
“The speeds are now where they need to be,” Zelensky said on social media, adding that restoration began overnight and was sufficient by Saturday morning, improving frontline logistics and defence against Russian jet-powered Shahed drones.
The restoration follows a new US diplomatic push to end the war. Russia agreed Wednesday to resume three-way negotiations with Washington and Kyiv next month.

articles.title_orig: Six Flags to add seat belts to roller coaster after Georgia man falls to his death
articles.title_zh: Six Flags to add seat belts to roller coaster after Georgia man falls to his death
articles.content_orig:
Six Flags said Friday that it will add seat belts to a roller coaster from which a man was ejected and fell to his death earlier this month.
In a press release, the theme park said it is adding seat belts to Goliath at Six Flags Over Georgia, outside Atlanta, as part of  broader new safety measures. Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem , 42, was ejected from the ride and fell to his death Oct. 12.
“I know trust is earned through actions and not words. As CEO of Six Flags, I take that responsibility personally,” John Reilly, Six Flags president and CEO, said in a statement. “We will continue to communicate about our progress and hold ourselves accountable to our commitments to you.”
Goliath remains closed, in addition to several other rides across five other parks “out of an abundance of caution.”
Six Flags did not immediately return a request for comment on which roller coasters remain closed or when they might reopen.
A company spokesperson previously said the following rides were closed shortly after the incident: Raging Bull at Six Flags Great America; Goliath at Six Flags Magic Mountain; Nitro at Six Flags Great Adventure; Leviathan and Behemoth at Canada’s Wonderland; Fury 325 and Thunder Striker at Carowinds; and Orion and Diamondback at Kings Island.
As of Friday, more than 220 of the company’s roller coasters remain in operation, according to Six Flags.
The company has “engaged independent engineers and ride inspection specialists to comprehensively review current safety procedures across our entire portfolio of rides and attractions, across all of our parks,” according to the press release.
Last week, the Georgia Office of Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire shared several “inspection details” reports for the Goliath roller coaster between 2014 and 2026.
The reports concern Goliath’s mechanical condition, structural supports, access areas and maintenance findings. They show that Goliath repeatedly passed annual inspections even as inspectors identified issues ranging from corrosion and worn drive wheels to issues involving ride supports and foundations.
The March 2026 inspection also resulted in a “pass,” although an inspector noted that bushings — which are specialized mechanical bearings used to absorb shock — needed to be replaced.
Kariem worked at Wesley International Academy in the Atlanta Public Schools district, the district said. His body hit other people on the ride before landing on the roof of a haunted house attraction below, according to witnesses .
The October incident was not the first time Six Flags’ roller coasters made headlines.
In September, Six Flags was sued by riders alleged that they suffered brain injuries on the X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain in Southern California. The ride features 360-degree rotating seats, a 215-foot drop and sudden flips and rotations.
I’m a reporter on NBC News’ breaking news team, covering crime, extreme weather, pop culture and more. I recently covered Hurricane Milton, which devastated the Tampa, Florida, metropolitan area, and the student-led protests at Columbia University.

articles.title_orig: Thousands rally in Tel Aviv against Netanyahu ahead of vote
articles.title_zh: Thousands rally in Tel Aviv against Netanyahu ahead of vote
articles.content_orig:
Thousands of Israelis are protesting against the government and calling for an independent inquiry into the security failures that led to the October 7, 2023 attacks .
Demonstrators rallied in the public plaza known as Hostages Square in Tel Aviv on Saturday, three days before Israel’s first general election since the genocidal war on Gaza began.
The protest was organised by the October Council, a group founded by the families of captives taken to Gaza three years ago, to demand accountability for the government’s failure to prevent the Hamas attack that preceded the war.
“Three days before the election, we will hold the culminating event marking three years of struggle to uncover the truth, demand accountability and establish a state commission of inquiry,” the October Council wrote on X ahead of the rally.
Elsewhere in Israel, protesters were also gathering for antigovernment demonstrations, reported Haaretz newspaper.
Taking part were leading figures from opposition parties, including Gadi Eisenkot of the Yashar party, who is Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s main centre-right rival.
In Tel Aviv, Eisenkot was greeted by chants of “Who’s coming? The next prime minister”, according to The Times of Israel. The leader of the Democrats, Yair Golan, was also at the rally.
“Masses, masses of masses, flowing in the ‘Democrats’ march from Rabin Square to the Hostages Square – for change, for hope, for r-e-v-o-l-u-t-i-o-n. What energy. This time it’s ours completely!”, Israeli citizen and lawyer Dan Adin posted on X.
Polls ahead of Tuesday’s election suggest a tight race, with Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc, in power since late 2022, neck and neck with Eisenkot’s. Neither bloc is currently projected to obtain a majority of seats in Israel’s parliament.
The election could be pivotal in determining whether Israel launches another round of strikes on Iran. Eisenkot is believed to be less inclined to resume military action against Tehran if he becomes Israel’s next prime minister.
However, on most other foreign policy issues, leading Israeli parties and politicians remain united, including in their opposition to the creation of an independent Palestinian state.
Ahead of the protest, the October Council alerted law enforcement to possible “provocations” from pro-government agitators.
“We have sent an urgent letter to the Police Commissioner following alerts about attempts by entities linked to the coalition to disrupt tonight’s rally,” it wrote on X.
The October Council aims to hold Israeli officials deemed responsible for the October 7 attacks to account and deliver justice for affected families.
Netanyahu’s coalition government, however, has refused demands to establish an independent commission of inquiry. Instead, it has offered to set up a “political” commission. Half of the commission’s members would be appointed by the government, while the remainder would be appointed by opposition legislators.
Opposition leaders have said they would boycott a commission appointed by politicians.

articles.title_orig: Husband's tribute to British woman who died after rescuing son in the Bahamas
articles.title_zh: Husband's tribute to British woman who died after rescuing son in the Bahamas
articles.content_orig:
The husband of a British woman who died rescuing their sons when they were swept away to sea in the Bahamas says she was a "hero... in life and in death".
Leanne Gregory, from Stapleford in Nottinghamshire, had been snorkelling with her family when the boys were swept away by a strong current, police said.
Although the children were rescued from the water off the island of Bimini on Tuesday, their mother was unable to be saved, the Royal Bahamas Police Force said.
Nathan Gregory said the loss of his 36-year-old "childhood sweetheart" was "unimaginable for our family".
"She was the purest, most amazing wife, mother and friend to have ever walked this Earth," her husband said in a Facebook post.
"I will never get over this, she was my soulmate, my childhood sweetheart, my one and only. The foundation of my entire family and the strength that held us all together.
"My boys had to witness something nobody should ever have to see of any age, but they know Mum died an absolute hero."
Gregory said he had also set up a fundraising page "for my sons and security after the tragic loss".
In the post on that page he described how his wife, who he had been with for 22 years, had held on to their son until he was rescued "but didn't have the energy to save herself".
He added: "I just have to be thankful for the hero she was in life and in death, and  totally grateful for the fact my boys got out safely."
In a statement posted on social media, the Royal Bahamas Police Force said officers  received reports shortly after 10:00 local time on Tuesday that a woman had been found unresponsive at the North Bimini Ferry Dock.
It added after she was swept away, she was brought to the ferry dock where CPR was given.
Mrs Gregory was then taken to a local medical clinic but was confirmed dead there, the police force said.
It said an autopsy would be conducted but "foul play is not suspected".
A spokesperson for the Foreign Office added: "Our thoughts are with the family of a British woman who has died in the Bahamas.
"We are in contact with the local authorities and providing support to her family."

articles.title_orig: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start amid high chocolate prices and affordability concerns
articles.title_zh: Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start amid high chocolate prices and affordability concerns
articles.content_orig:
Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start this year as U.S. consumers grapple with high living costs and eye-popping chocolate prices .
Halloween candy sales fell 6.7% in the month ending Oct. 17 compared to the same period last year, according to NielsenIQ, a market research firm. Nielsen also noted an 11.7% decline in candy sales in mid-September, erasing the preseason gains that Halloween candy enjoyed the previous two years.
Chris Costagli, a vice president and food thought leader at NielsenIQ, said high gas prices have worsened Americans’ concerns about affordability, and that’s dampening demand for Halloween treats. As of Friday, the average price of a gallon of regular gasoline in the U.S. was $4.29, up nearly 40% from the prior year.
“I think what you’re seeing now is a consumer that’s spending so much additional money on fuel and housing and clothing and food,” Costagli said. “Some of the decisions they’re making about Halloween candy, it’s not necessarily because, ‘I notice it’s more expensive than last year,’ it’s, ‘I can’t afford it this year because I’ve paid so much more for so many other things. I just don’t have the financial means to buy it this year.’”
Small bags of candy were the only sizes seeing sales growth through mid-October, Costagli noted. Large and extra-large bags were seeing the biggest declines.
U.S. candy prices have been climbing faster than the rate of inflation for several years. As of September, candy and gum prices were up 44% over a five-year period, according to government data. Prices for all food eaten at home rose 22.5% in the same period.
This week, discount grocer Aldi was advertising a 135-piece variety pack of Mars Inc. chocolate bars — including Milky Way, Trix and Snickers — for $19.87. That’s almost the same price consumers paid for a 250-piece variety pack five years ago.
Cocoa prices are the main culprit. Global cocoa prices reached a record high of $10,710 per metric ton in January 2025 because of poor weather in West Africa — which supplies 70% of the world’s chocolate -- and speculative trading in the cocoa futures market, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Cocoa prices had been falling steadily since then, and hit $3,241 per metric ton in March. But they began climbing again in the spring as the Iran war disrupted Africa’s fertilizer supplies . The El Niño weather pattern is also expected to hurt production, with hot, dry conditions expected through February.
But Costagli noted that even in cases where prices are lower than last year, consumer demand is muted. The average price of non-chocolate Halloween candies , like gummies and lollipops, was $6.08 per pound in the nine weeks ending Oct. 17, which was about 3% lower than last year, according to Nielsen data. But that didn’t lead to a bump in sales.
Sally Lyons Wyatt, a global executive vice president and food industry adviser for the market research company Circana, said one way U.S. consumers have been handling higher grocery prices is by making smaller and more frequent trips to the supermarket and buying products right before they intend to use them. That makes her wonder if shoppers are waiting until closer to Halloween to buy candy this year.
“People are very intentional and thoughtful about what they want to consume, not just for holidays, but in general,” she said. “I do believe we will still see softness overall with candy, but I don’t think Halloween is doomed.”
The National Confectioners Association, a trade group that represents candy makers like Mars, Smarties Candy Co. and Ferrara Candy Co., said it remains optimistic about Halloween sales.
“We are just now entering the peak period for Halloween and consumer enthusiasm remains incredibly strong,” the group said Friday in a statement.

Coverage for this event has ended.
An Israeli special operations veteran urged the United States and Israel on Friday to focus future military strikes on preventing Iran from rebuilding its nuclear and missile capabilities.
Aaron Cohen, founder of Gideon, told FOX Business' "Kudlow" that previous U.S. and Israeli operations had significantly weakened Iran's military infrastructure, but warned that Tehran could restore its capabilities without continued pressure.
Cohen pointed to reported activity at Iran's underground Eagle 44 military base and changes in the country's defense leadership as possible signs of rebuilding efforts. He argued that future operations should prioritize disrupting Iran's ability to replenish military equipment and infrastructure.
His comments come as President Donald Trump has raised the possibility of additional strikes against Iran following the November midterm elections, although no new military operation has been announced.
Brent crude briefly topped $117 a barrel Friday as uncertainty surrounding the Iran conflict continued to weigh on global energy markets.
The international oil benchmark settled at $116.72 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate, the U.S. benchmark, closed at $103.27 after climbing above $103 during the trading session.
The latest price movements come as commercial vessels continue to face security threats in the Strait of Hormuz, a major shipping corridor for global oil supplies.
President Donald Trump's administration has maintained a naval blockade targeting Iranian oil exports, while the president has left open the possibility of additional military strikes against Tehran.
International nuclear inspectors could play a central role in a future agreement between the United States and Iran, with the United Nations ' nuclear watchdog signaling Friday that it has completed much of the preparation needed to verify Tehran's nuclear activities.
Rafael Grossi, director general of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), told the U.N. General Assembly in New York that the agency is prepared to carry out independent monitoring if Washington and Tehran reach a diplomatic agreement.
Grossi emphasized that a lasting resolution to the dispute over Iran's nuclear program would require international oversight, making verification a key component of any potential deal.
The IAEA chief also expressed optimism about diplomatic efforts involving Pakistan, Qatar, Oman and Egypt, which have supported negotiations between the United States and Iran.
His remarks come as President Donald Trump has raised the possibility of additional military strikes against Iran if Tehran does not reach an agreement with Washington.
While the IAEA says its technical preparations are largely complete, no new agreement authorizing inspections has been announced.
Russian President Vladimir Putin is preparing to host Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Moscow next week, adding another round of high-level diplomacy between the two countries as Tehran faces continued U.S. military and economic pressure.
The upcoming visit was confirmed by Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, Reuters reported. It comes just days after Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov traveled to Tehran for discussions with Iranian officials.
The diplomatic activity highlights the close relationship between Moscow and Tehran, even as President Donald Trump has questioned how much assistance Russia is providing Iran during the conflict.
Araghchi has maintained that relations between the two countries are stronger than ever, according to Reuters.
The meeting would mark Pezeshkian's first visit with Putin in Russia since the conflict began, although the two leaders have held talks elsewhere in recent months, including in Turkmenistan earlier in October and Kyrgyzstan in September.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday that oil exports from the Persian Gulf have rebounded above pre-conflict levels despite Iran's efforts to disrupt energy shipments through the region.
In a post on X, Bessent shared a Treasury Department chart showing crude oil and condensate exports through the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman and the Red Sea recovering to approximately 17 million to 18 million barrels per day.
The chart shows shipments plunged earlier this year before gradually recovering, with the latest figures exceeding the January-February 2026 average.
Bessent credited the rebound as evidence that Iran has failed to halt energy shipments to international markets despite attacks on commercial vessels and continued tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.
The development comes as the Trump administration maintains economic pressure on Tehran through a U.S. naval blockade aimed at restricting Iranian oil exports while allowing other energy shipments to continue.
A 2014 conference in Tehran attended by Code Pink co-founder Medea Benjamin was later sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury Department over allegations that it helped Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) recruit foreign intelligence assets, according to a report by The Telegraph.
The Treasury Department sanctioned the New Horizon organization in 2019, accusing it of facilitating intelligence gathering and recruitment on behalf of the IRGC's Quds Force.
Benjamin was photographed at the conference with Nader Talebzadeh and Hamed Ghashghavi, two men whom U.S. authorities later identified as intermediaries involved in identifying potential foreign recruits, The Telegraph reported.
The report also cited an intelligence source who alleged that Iran considered Benjamin an asset because of her public advocacy. The characterization does not, by itself, establish that Benjamin knowingly cooperated with Iranian intelligence.
Benjamin returned to Iran in 2019 as part of a 28-member Code Pink delegation that met with then-Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif.
Internet connectivity across the Persian Gulf could face disruptions if fighting between Iran and the United States resumes, with Iranian security officials reportedly considering attacks on underwater communications cables.
The potential consequences could be concentrated in the region rather than felt worldwide. Alan Mauldin, research director at telecommunications research firm TeleGeography, told Reuters that less than 1% of international bandwidth passes through the Strait of Hormuz.
The assessment comes as two senior Iranian security officials told Reuters that Tehran has prepared plans to damage undersea communications infrastructure in response to renewed U.S. and Israeli military strikes.
One official also described plans to interfere with repairs, potentially extending service disruptions. Neither official identified specific cables or explained how Iran would carry out the attacks.
The reported threat comes as President Donald Trump has suggested the U.S. could launch additional military operations against Iran if Tehran does not reach an agreement with Washington.
Internet and telecommunications networks in the Persian Gulf could become targets of Iranian retaliation if President Donald Trump orders additional military strikes against Tehran, according to a Reuters report Friday.
Two senior Iranian security officials told the news agency that Tehran has prepared contingency plans involving underwater communications cables, potentially threatening connectivity across the region.
The reported plans also include obstructing repairs to damaged infrastructure, which could extend disruptions to internet and other communications services.
The warning comes as Trump has raised the possibility of another round of Operation Epic Fury strikes against Iran , suggesting Friday that additional military action remains an option if Tehran does not reach an agreement with Washington.

articles.title_orig: The Rare-Earth Vultures Harvesting Metals From America’s Old Wind Turbines
articles.title_zh: The Rare-Earth Vultures Harvesting Metals From America’s Old Wind Turbines
articles.content_orig:
The technologies transforming modern industry depend on materials that rarely receive the same attention as the innovations they make possible. Artificial intelligence, robotics, electric vehicles, advanced aerospace systems, and high-performance electronics all rely on sophisticated components whose production requires access to specialized minerals.
Perhaps the most strategically important are rare earth elements, particularly those used in high-performance permanent magnets. And while the technology industry continues pushing the boundaries of what machines can accomplish, another challenge is gaining urgency: finding dependable new sources of the materials needed to manufacture them.
China dominates much of the world’s rare earth processing and magnet production, creating a concentrated supply chain that governments and manufacturers are increasingly determined to diversify.
That effort is directing attention toward resource-rich countries such as Brazil. But discovering new mineral deposits is only part of the solution.
The next important technological advances may come from finding better ways to recover the minerals already being discovered.
Why Rare Earth Recovery Technology Matters
Rare earth elements aren’t necessarily rare in Earth’s crust. The difficulty often lies in identifying deposits with useful concentrations of valuable elements and developing efficient methods to separate and recover them.
Terbium and dysprosium illustrate the challenge. These heavy rare earth elements help certain permanent magnets retain their strength at elevated temperatures, making them valuable in electric vehicle motors, industrial robotics, wind turbines, and aerospace equipment.
For manufacturers, access to these materials is closely connected to product performance and supply reliability. For companies developing new mineral resources, the question becomes how to extract them in ways that are technically practical, environmentally manageable, and potentially commercially viable.
One area attracting attention is ionic adsorption clay, a type of rare earth-bearing deposit in which certain elements can be recovered through chemical leaching.
Unlike conventional hard-rock mining, some ionic clay deposits may offer opportunities to investigate alternative extraction approaches, potentially reducing the amount of material that must be excavated and processed.
And in Brazil, researchers are exploring what those possibilities could mean for future rare earth supplies.
A Brazilian Project Combining Scale With Technical Progress
Among the companies investigating these opportunities is IMC Rare Earths Ltd. (NYSE American: IMC), which is advancing its Itarantim rare earth project across portions of Bahia and Minas Gerais.
Itarantim hosts a reported 1.1-billion-tonne inferred mineral resource containing the four principal magnet rare earth elements: neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium.
That geological scale provides a strong foundation for exploration, but it’s the company’s recent metallurgical testing that adds another dimension to the project.
In September, laboratory work conducted with Brazil’s IFRN and CT Mineral reported terbium recovery reaching 95.2% in the best-performing test , with an average recovery of 81.1% in the reported composite. The company also produced a mixed rare earth carbonate, an intermediate material that can be further processed into separated rare earth products.
Separate research at the University of Brighton in the United Kingdom recovered 73% of the total rare earth elements tested, excluding cerium, using an acidified magnesium sulfate solution. The same testing recovered 71.4% of terbium and 70.5% of dysprosium.
These results were obtained under different laboratory conditions and should not be treated as interchangeable recovery rates. Nevertheless, they show how Itarantim’s mineralization responds to potential extraction methods.
And that information is central to evaluating what comes next.
Could Rare Earths Be Recovered Through Wells?
One of the more intriguing possibilities emerging from testing is in-situ recovery .
Rather than excavating large volumes of rare earth-bearing clay, the proposed method involves injecting a suitable solution through injection wells, letting it interact with the mineralized material, and recovering the resulting rare earth-bearing liquid through extraction wells.
The minerals would then undergo further processing to produce intermediate materials suitable for eventual refining.
If successfully demonstrated under field conditions, this approach could potentially reduce excavation, material transportation, and the need for extensive tailings storage. It might also offer advantages in surface disturbance and infrastructure requirements compared with certain conventional mining methods.
The technology is not yet commercially validated at Itarantim. Field testing must establish whether fluids can move effectively through the deposit, remain controlled, and be recovered reliably.
But the laboratory findings provide a reason to investigate those possibilities further.
Another encouraging observation concerns the composition of the recovered solutions. In the University of Brighton tests, uranium and thorium remained below detection limits in the leachate. IMC has also reported negligible deleterious elements in certain tested solutions.
These results do not establish that the entire deposit is free of radioactivity. They do, however, provide potentially useful information for researchers, regulators, and development partners assessing processing requirements, environmental considerations, and future waste management.
As the technology becomes increasingly focused on efficiency and resource management, those characteristics could become important as testing advances.
New Discoveries Expand the Scientific Questions
While the metallurgical work continues, IMC is also investigating mineralization beyond its existing resource boundaries.
On October 8, the company announced a new high-grade, terbium-rich zone at Block H, where drilling identified seven meters of mineralization beginning just two meters below the surface, including a higher-grade three-meter section.
Preliminary testing recovered 64% to 83% of terbium from samples taken from the upper portion of the enriched zone.
The discovery lies outside Itarantim’s currently defined resource, creating another area for exploration. At Block D, drilling has also identified 20 meters of continuous mineralization, with additional work planned to investigate its extent.
Together, these findings are helping researchers examine both the deposit’s geological characteristics and recovery methods suitable for different mineralized areas.
IMC has engaged ANSTO Minerals in Australia for further metallurgical studies and is evaluating potential processing approaches, including in-situ, vat, and heap leaching.
Next stages will include additional resource definition, engineering evaluation, field testing, and potential partnerships with industrial and government organizations that can support future development.
The Technology Behind a More Diversified Supply Chain
The global effort to diversify rare earth supplies is often discussed in terms of geopolitics and mineral discoveries. Yet processing technology may prove equally important.
A large mineral resource cannot contribute to manufacturing supply chains unless its valuable elements can be recovered, refined, and delivered in forms that industry can use.
That makes the work taking place at projects such as Itarantim relevant beyond the mining sector. Laboratory research, chemical processing, geological modeling, and engineering innovation all support efforts to establish new sources of materials essential to advanced technology.

articles.title_orig: Rubio calls on Cubans seeking "positive change" to work with CIA: "Now is the time"
articles.title_zh: Rubio calls on Cubans seeking "positive change" to work with CIA: "Now is the time"
articles.content_orig:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on Cubans seeking "positive change" to work with the CIA, the latest ploy in the growing efforts from the Trump administration to remove Cuba's communist regime from power.
"To those who seek to create positive change in Cuba - now is the time," Rubio wrote Friday on X. "The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete partnership with the CIA."
Shortly afterward, the CIA reposted Rubio's message and a similar call in Spanish for Cubans to work with the agency. A video was posted alongside the message showing the steps needed to contact the intelligence agency.
A strict U.S. embargo and sanctions seeking to put pressure on Cuba's communist government have led to prices of basic goods skyrocketing and decreased access to medical care for its citizens. Cubans reported waiting in bread lines for hours and others reported lining up to see a doctor.
Last week, the U.S. government announced additional economic sanctions on Cuba's state-run bank, saying the institution had ties to Iran.
President Trump said on Friday during a campaign rally in South Florida that "we'll take care of Cuba on our way back from Iran." He was referring to the U.S. Navy warships deployed near the Strait of Hormuz.
Mr. Trump added: "Those beautiful ships will pass Cuba. We'll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They'll raise up their hands, and then we're going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal."
Cuba's government has pushed back, with Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla responding Friday on X , saying: "We reject any threats stemming from U.S. ambitions toward Cuba."
Rodriguez Parrilla added: "Our shores are lined with beautiful beaches, but they are also rugged and inhospitable to those who arrive with hostile intentions and a desire for domination."
Olivia  Gazis contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: 61 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's 'Halloween Sale' (Europe)
articles.title_zh: 61 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's 'Halloween Sale' (Europe)
articles.content_orig:
After Nintendo of America launched its ' Screaming Deals ' sale earlier this week, we knew it wouldn't be long before Europe followed suit.
The 'Halloween Sale' is now live for those in Europe, with delicious discounts on a boatload of titles available until 1st November . So, naturally, we have assembled the following list to make things a little more manageable.
Below, you will find every game in the Halloween Sale that we rated a 9/10 or higher, plus a personal pick from all the games that fall below this review bar. We've listed things alphabetically and given the discounted price, so you know what you're paying for each.
Subscribe to Nintendo Life on YouTube 854k
As ever, if you're looking to grab some eShop credit before diving in, we've got you covered with the following links from our store .
Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.
Alien: Isolation is a survival horror masterpiece and straight-up one of the very best horror video games ever released.
It's a nerve-wracking affair — a slow, methodical game of cat and mouse against a brilliantly clever recreation of one of cinema's most infamous killers — but if you're up to the task you'll find one of the most satisfying gameplay experiences in the genre; a brilliant and beautiful homage to one of the greatest sci-fi movies of all time.
Feral Interactive has done a stellar job with this Switch port and the excellent motion controls and inclusion of all previously-released DLC only go to sweeten the deal. This is essential stuff for survival horror fans.
Developer Shared Memory's stated goal was “to craft complete experiences that will be playable long after the world loses its internet connection,” and screen after screen, Animal Well excels in delighting your eyes and giving your brain something to stew on.
It’s a riposte against a culture of post-launch updates in favour of a meticulously crafted, singular vision with potentially years’ worth of discoveries baked in. By all indications, Animal Well delivers on that long-term promise and does so with a one-of-a-kind elegance.
BlazBlue CentralFiction Special Edition may have arrived a few years late on Switch, but that delay didn't dull the sharpness of its 2D fighting package.
Not only does it give the Ragna saga a proper send-off with a story mode that's so rich in character development it could be a full anime season in its own right, but it offers a staggering number of modes to keep you playing long after the credits roll. It runs silky-smooth docked or in handheld modes and runs like a dream online.
The lack of an English dub still rankles, and new adopters are going to have to do a lot of research to understand what's going on, but it's well worth the effort.
BlazBlue: Cross Tag Battle is an utterly accomplished 2D fighting game. It's bursting with content and featuring the visual spectacle of combat that uses up every single trick in the book. A few strange decisions aside, this title is a must for fighting game fans.
Even if you're not a fan of any of the franchises represented in this game, you most certainly will be by the time you're done with this stacked fighting package.
If Blue Prince were only about finding Room 46 and nabbing your inheritance, it would be a neat little puzzler with some fun twists along the way. For those who dive in headfirst and keep track of everything else it throws at you, however, it is so much more than that.
Rarely has a game made us feel more clever, more lost, and more elated the deeper into it we ventured, and still some question marks remain over its deeper mysteries. Minor technical drops and a lack of cross-save aside, this remains a superb achievement and one of the finest head scratchers we've had the pleasure of playing.
It looks like The Witness and it plays a bit like StreetPass Garden , but Botany Manor blooms into something that's not only entirely its own, but also something quite special. Don't let its cosy aesthetics fool you — Botany Manor is packed with nicely challenging, well-designed puzzles, and isn't afraid to tackle heavy subjects, too.
Chained Echoes is a wonderful mash-up of '90s JRPG tropes, masterfully woven together to produce an experience that feels simultaneously nostalgic and fresh. A well-paced story, unconventional progression system, tactical combat system, and expansive world all come together to make for a game that is shockingly one of the very best RPGs that we played in 2022.
Really, there’s no place where it feels like Chained Echoes drops the ball, which is all the more impressive when you consider that the vast majority of it was put together by one person. It stands as a shining example of everything that makes RPGs great.
As an adventure game, Chicory: A Colorful Tale is quite sincerely up there with the very best of the genre.
There’s plenty to see and do and a full completion run will probably take you 25-30 hours. The characters and their travails are rich and likeable, the game’s sense of humour is generally inspired, and it’s all very sweet without being sugary-twee and talking down to the player. It’s also an affecting little tearjerker that will definitely strike a chord if you make art, and almost certainly will even if you don’t – so long as you’re capable of pretty basic empathy.
Chicory is simple to play but impressively long and complex, with perfect controls, performance and visuals. Throw yourself into painting the world and you’ll be left with a game that’s very much your own and speaks to you directly – a beautiful marriage of mechanics, themes and visuals.
While it’s a shame that there are fewer games here than in other Konami collections — we’d have loved to have seen NES title Contra Force or the now-extinct WiiWare title Contra ReBirth — the ones included in the Contra Anniversary Collection are universally brilliant. The 8-bit and 16-bit Contra games are among the finest examples of the run ‘n gun genre, and to have almost all of them included in a single release and emulated flawlessly is an absolute treat.
Whether you’re a fan of the series or a curious onlooker who’s always wanted to see what the fuss was all about, this is essential.
We really like Crawl , and we’d bet our collected stash of gold and wrath you will, too. A dungeon-crawling hack-and-slash affair with roguelike elements, one player is the hero trying to get through a dungeon and the others play as monster-controlling ghosts attempting to kill said hero and take their place.
It's an everyone-for-themselves free-for-all, yet there are opportunities for frantic 3v1 co-operative play — a necessity when all the non-hero ghost characters must take joint control of bosses the hero faces. It’s great fun in single-player thanks to some aggressive AI, but that consistent danger takes on a new dimension when you and three of your friends are jostling for XP and that all-important killing blow.
Competitive couchplay doesn’t get much better than this on Switch.
A roguelike at heart with a rhythm-game soul, Crypt Of The NecroDancer is a sublime experience that’s a must-play for fans of the genre(s).
Its upbeat, uptempo take on dungeon crawling is infectious, and there’s enough content here to last even the savviest of spelunkers for many, many dance-fuelled dives into the depths. If you’ve never tangoed with the NecroDancer, this fully-featured Switch edition is the perfect way to jump in.
For anybody who never played this but loved the Zelda spin-off Cadence of Hyrule and was left wanting more, what are you waiting for?

articles.title_orig: New ‘Mass Effect 5’ Details Emerge After Cancellation, And It Sounds Great
articles.title_zh: New ‘Mass Effect 5’ Details Emerge After Cancellation, And It Sounds Great
articles.content_orig:
Those mourning yesterday’s shuttering of highly praised and influential developer BioWare also had to deal with the cancellation of the next Mass Effect game, which was first teased back in 2020 . Today, we got our best look at what that game could have been with a short, leaked trailer for Mass Effect: Universe .
In the roughly two-minute montage—which describes itself as “in-engine footage from our small team” that “uses our pre-production assets”—an ex-military officer wearing an N7 trenchcoat (similar to the one seen in that 2020 teaser) encounters an Asari at a bar. He talks of his frustration with military life—“by the time you put out one fire, another had already started”—before discussing his new line of work “stopping [the fires] before they start” and “making the choices no one else is willing to make. Going where others are afraid to go.”
Mass Effect: Universe Trailer by u/Random_Hyabusa_Ninja in masseffect
As the intriguing Asari at the bar reveals herself to be the one who metaphorically “start[s] the fires,” N7 allies reveal themselves as backup. The cutscene transitions seamlessly into an all-out group gunfight in the bar, complete with hostiles being stuck in place inside mass effect fields and others being crushed by furniture brought down on top of them.
The action-packed bar scene is interspersed with short vignettes from around the game’s universe, including a hovercraft speeding over an icy planet, an examination of a truly gigantic alien suspended in a glass cylinder, and a team looking at a holographic map dotted with dozens of points of interest.
The existence of the internal Mass Effect: Universe trailer was first revealed by an anonymous Reddit poster yesterday and then confirmed by IGN early Thursday morning. The trailer video appeared on Reddit slightly before noon Eastern time, with mods there saying they couldn’t “independently verify the authenticity” but that it “seems legitimate.” Within hours, both IGN and Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier had confirmed that the trailer was authentic and came from someone inside EA.
Following yesterday’s BioWare closure announcement, sci-fi authors Catherynne M. Valente and Derek Kunsken both revealed they had been working on the game for years. “It was one of the greatest privileges & GLORIOUS challenges of my life. I smiled every day. I worked HARD for the fans, every day,” Valente wrote. “What we were cooking was really cool,” Kunsken added.
Despite the existence of a 6-year-old teaser for the game, EA executives Cam Weber and David Tinson said in a memo to staff yesterday that there was only “a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect .” The decision “not to move forward with this development” led to BioWare’s closure, which the note calls “a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly.”
In an N7 Day blog post last year , Executive Producer Mike Gamble said, “The team is heads-down and focused exclusively on Mass Effect . We have a lot of universe to cover, lots of features to build, and lots of romances to figure out. We’re excited by what we’re building, and we promise you: when we’re ready, it’ll be a lot of fun to show.”
“Your support has meant everything to me over the past 17 years at BioWare,” Gamble wrote yesterday on social media .
Despite the game’s cancellation, the Mass Effect universe will still be represented on streaming TV screens. IGN cites “sources inside Prime Video” in reporting that the streaming series first announced in 2024 is still in active development.
As for the series’s future in gaming, an Internet petition has predictably popped up urging EA to continue funding development of the series or license the IP to an outside studio. The petition has nearly 17,500 signatories as of this writing, though those petitioners face an uphill battle convincing EA’s new private ownership to focus on a massive narrative action RPG and not more profitable franchises like Battlefield , The Sims , and annual sports releases.

Where are the criminals you said you were going to arrest? Yes, thereâs a few that youâve done, but the majority have been hardworking people.â
She continued, âHardworking women. I just want to tear upâwomen that Iâve seen with their children, walking every day to school. Whereâs your mom? Kids staying behindâbroken families, it is just heartbreaking.â

Trumpâs violent crackdown, which has reportedly led to around 980,000 people being deported , most of whom have no criminal record, has sparked regret among many Trump voters who wanted to see criminals removed from the countryânot innocent families violently split apart.
Benny Melendez, who has installed fences on construction sites he manages to protect his workers from ICE, says he also regrets voting for Trumpâjust as he regretted voting for Biden in 2020.
Melendez tells CBS News that so many arrests in his Texas community have made it hard to find workers, and building a house can take twice as long because of a lack of manpower. According to TRAC , Texas, a state that has voted for Trump in all three of his presidential elections, has more immigration detentions than any other state.
Trumpâs approval rating has fallen to a record low of 32 percent, according to CNN , just weeks ahead of the midterms that are expected to be a bloodbath for Republicans, who are at serious risk of losing their majorities in both the House and Senate.
The economy has proven to be the most stubborn issue for most Americans, with two-thirds of voters, and one-third of Republicans , saying the president has made economic conditions worse.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stands with White House Border Czar Tom Homan, and Attorney General Pam Bondi before former U.S. Sen. Markwayne Mullin is sworn in as the next secretary of the Department of Homeland Security in the Oval Office at the White House on March 24, 2026.
Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images
While polling has suggested that immigration is unlikely to be a definitional issue ahead of Novemberâs elections, Michigan State University political scientist Matthew Grossman told The Guardian that Trumpâs deportation policies were part of a general feeling of the president having â gone too far ,â a sentiment also seen in terms of the Iran war and tariffs .
However, the issue hasnât fazed White House border czar Tom Homan: âMy job as a border czar is to keep that border secure and enforce immigration law,â he told CBS News earlier this month. âI particularly donât care about midterms.â

articles.title_orig: These clever apps show off the iPhone Duo’s potential
articles.title_zh: These clever apps show off the iPhone Duo’s potential
articles.content_orig:
Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.
Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW.
It’s been a long time since I’ve been genuinely excited about a new iPhone.
For years, a new iPhone meant a device that was thinner, faster, and had a camera that came with incredible upgrades. At some point (and Apple devotees can debate which year’s model this was!), a new iPhone became an incremental upgrade. Slightly better, slightly faster. Maybe there was a new button to learn, a new charging cable , or a new notch on the screen , but the iPhone itself remained the same rectangular glass and metal handheld it always was.
The iPhone Duo changes this, allowing Apple to enter the market for foldable phones with a phone that, while imperfect , is whimsical, fun, and, yes, actually exciting.
It’s hard to say when the urge to acquire the iPhone Duo first kicked in. I’ll admit that it wasn’t during the official announcement , which left me feeling puzzled about the device’s potential. Do I actually want a phone that folds, I wondered? Was propping up the phone as a little tent to watch Netflix worth all that extra money? (The Duo starts at $2,000).
As it turned out, the desire for the Duo grew on me as I saw developers embracing the new foldable design to create Duo-optimized apps. Apple’s software development community, after all, is what keeps me locked into the iPhone. Apple developers are active, creative, engaged, and still often build for iOS first – a must if you like trying things early.
Of course, the initial Duo reviews have pointed out how many mainstream iOS apps have not yet been made ready for the Duo, which is true. Many of the apps you use every day were not optimized by launch day, meaning they’re surrounded by black bars, have their controls in odd places, or have to be enlarged with a tap, similar to the early days of running iPhone apps on iPad.
But the developers who have specifically built for the Duo sparked my interest. Soon, my inbox was filled with pitches for clever apps I couldn’t yet try unless I got my hands on a Duo. Hello, FOMO.
The best of these don’t just adapt their apps to display correctly on the foldable form factor, but make use of the fact that there are different displays of different sizes – and they incorporate that into the design of the apps themselves.
Below are some of my early favorites, tested on a review unit provided by Apple.
Let’s start with the basics. Netflix is one of Apple’s hand-picked partners for the Duo launch, and had its streaming app Duo-optimized by the time the device shipped, alongside others like the MLB app, NYT Cooking, Slack, my preferred calendar app Fantastical , and others. But Netflix is the perfect showcase for what I expect will be a regular Duo use case: watching movies and TV.
The streaming app hasn’t just been expanded to fill the screen; it takes advantage of the fact that there are two different screen sizes to build for. On the outer screen (the display you see when the device is folded), you can scroll through Netflix’s short-form, TikTok-like “Clips,” then open up the device to continue watching videos on the larger matte-screen inner display. The transition between the two experiences feels as seamless as unfolding the Duo itself, as the content automatically adapts to the new screen size.
As I personally find myself watching most TV on my phone these days, as opposed to big screen in the living room, I appreciate having the option to shift from a phone to a larger screen with one device. This is going to be one of my most-used apps, I think.
Look, I called it back in September. I have to credit Deck-Man , which was previously known as Duo-Man, as being the first app that made me want to get a Duo. Designed by indie developer Vidit Bhargava at a hackathon, the music player takes clever advantage of the Duo’s two screens to imitate how Walkman cassette players used to function.
The playful app reimagines the cassette player as a digital experience with retro vibes, allowing you to browse through your favorite albums as cassettes, then load them into the player. You can then control the playback with play, pause, fast-forward, and rewind controls, as you would on a hardware device, complete with authentic-sounding clicks and cassette sounds that were recorded from a real portable cassette player.
With the Duo open, the cassette appears to play on the right side of the screen, next to album imagery on the right. When closed, Deck-Man’s interface looks like the front of a Walkman.
The app has appeal not only because it built something that could only exist on a hinged, foldable device like the Duo, but also because it taps into the growing demand for retro tech , which is partly a cultural response to the speed at which the AI industry is shipping out products. Retro tech , like dumbphones , digital cameras, vinyl, CDs , and landlines, recalls an older time when tech use was intentional, not just baked into every aspect of our lives.
Honestly, if you buy a Duo and don’t install Deck-Man, I’m convinced you just don’t know how to have fun.
Duo-Man is now Deck-Man! Expanding my app to have a unique experience on all platforms and not just the Duo, so it only makes sense to have a better name reflecting that. See you October 23 on the App Store! pic.twitter.com/kCdjcmbeGG
The TypeDraw app is designed to be a personal notebook, something that looks like a virtual Moleskine of sorts — it even has an elastic closure band. But there’s a certain charm to using this app specifically on the Duo, whose form factor makes it look a lot like a little notebook when closed.
Inside TypeDraw, you can type using a font that’s your own handwriting or pick from one of a dozen fonts designed by its creator, Phil Traut.
You can also choose which kind of paper you want to write on, like lined, grid, or dotted pages, and pick your ink color. You can also draw and sketch to create colorful images that accompany your handwritten text, which makes it feel a lot more like using a real-life notebook as your journal or diary, and not some boring to-do app.
The pages curl as you flip through them, and you can even pull on the elastic band to produce a twang animation that’s just silly and fun.
I turned iPhone Duo into a real-life notebook where you can type anywhere in your own handwriting or with one of 12 fonts I designed myself. Type or draw, then close it. The next time you open the book, it shows your most recent note or the one captured nearest to your current… pic.twitter.com/d23kMbj8TH
Wakeout , the workout app that’s a former Apple App of the Year winner, has also approached its Duo optimization thoughtfully by designing different user interfaces for each postion the phone can be in. The app, which offers a series of mini movement breaks that feel more like games than exercise, works when the Duo is closed, open, in tent mode, or sitting open like a laptop computer.
For instance, when the Duo is open like a book, the view is split across the hinge with the movement game videos on the left, but when it’s open like a laptop, the videos shift to the vertical screen. You can also put it into tent mode, which is great for watching the videos with the Duo propped up on your desk. (Most people use Wakeout at work, when they take quick stretch breaks after sitting at a desk for too long.)
If the app is running on a closed Duo, its row of navigation tabs becomes a slim side menu in the column beside the camera, allowing the phone’s small screen to use the full display.
Already my favorite travel app, Apple Design Award-winning Flighty tells you everything you need to know about your upcoming flight, from gate updates to delays to airport conditions and even the type of aircraft you’re flying.
But on the iPhone Duo, when open, the app takes advantage of the expanded screen space to spread its map to the edges, letting you see more of your fli

articles.title_orig: Gamers are now playing Steam games directly on PlayStation 5, no streaming required
articles.title_zh: Gamers are now playing Steam games directly on PlayStation 5, no streaming required
articles.content_orig:
PlayStation 5 owners are beginning to run Windows PC games from their Steam libraries directly on jailbroken consoles. Unlike Remote Play or cloud gaming, the games are executed locally using the PS5 hardware. Several projects now support this functionality, although game compatibility and performance remain limited.
One recent demonstration comes from X user ‘v7dt1’, who shared footage of a Steam booting into UI on his PlayStation 5. He explained that the game was downloaded from Steam and executed directly on the console. However, he also admitted that the game eventually crashed and that getting everything to work remains difficult. The exact software used in his demonstration has not been confirmed. It appears that this user is using something called Playden for PS5.
One of the projects making this possible is Playden for PS5 . First made publicly available earlier this month, Playden allows users to sign in to Steam, browse their libraries, download games and launch them directly from the PS5 home screen. It uses prospero-win, a port of Wine for PlayStation 5, rather than requiring a separate Linux installation.
The software supports Direct3D 8 through 11 using DXVK, while Direct3D 12 games use VKD3D-Proton. According to the project’s compatibility database, games such as Cyberpunk 2077, Hollow Knight, Cuphead, Portal 2, Dead Cells and Deep Rock Galactic have reached playable states. Cyberpunk 2077 was tested for 13 minutes with a controller, although no frame rate measurements were provided. These results should not be interpreted as confirmation that the games work without problems.
Playden has already received several updates, with version 0.6.0 arriving this week. The latest update adds support for importing Windows games from USB storage or FTP, 120 Hz output and additional display settings. However, online multiplayer remains unsupported, and games requiring third-party launchers or certain anti-cheat systems cannot run.
Here’s an actual demo featuring Potal on PlayStation through Playden:
Testing Steam games on Playden! by u/Cevap in PS5_Jailbreak
Worth adding that this is not Steam running inside Linux on PS5. There is no need to boot into Linux, as Playden runs as a native PS5 application accessible from the console’s home screen. However, multiplayer games are not currently supported, and users should be cautious about connecting their Steam accounts to experimental software. Also, this should be obvious, but Playden requires a jailbroken PS5.

articles.title_orig: Swap The Bathtub Curtain: Add Privacy With An Amazon Alternative
articles.title_zh: Swap The Bathtub Curtain: Add Privacy With An Amazon Alternative
articles.content_orig:
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
Shower curtains are a solid option for many bathrooms, but they aren't always the best choice. In the wrong room, they can make the space feel small, get in the way while you're cleaning, or become pretty gross. If you're tired of clingy fabric, but still need a little privacy, the Frosted Bathtub Shower Door by EGrinbey on Amazon is a potential swap for a shower curtain , with the frost adding a layer of protection compared to clear ones.
This product is minimal enough that you can easily fit it in most bathrooms. It features lightly frosted glass and sleek, black hardware for something simple and elegant. According to the Amazon page, the door should work for any opening measuring 56-60 inches wide and 60 inches tall. However, the seller does note that the lower slider is 1.9 inches wide. Whatever you are installing the door on top of, you have to make sure it is wider than that for it to fit properly.
Cost is one of the important things to consider before installing a new shower door . Thankfully, while it is certainly expensive compared to a cheap plastic film, it is under $400, which is a steal compared to having a professional do the work. "Awesome shower door for the money," said a 5-star reviewer on Amazon .
This shower door is relatively easy to install, even for a beginner. However, you do have to cut and drill in the right spots to get everything in the correct placement and prevent leaks. When cutting, measure the total length for your shower space and the metal carefully. The same goes for marking where you need to drill holes; double-check that everything is in the right position before you mark anything. It's always a good idea to read through the instructions in preparation for starting a project, but especially in this case, as a mistake could make the whole door impossible to use for your bathroom.
Patience is also key. As you install this product, you want to be careful not to damage the doors in any way. There is something known as the exploding glass shower door phenomenon . Though this is SGCC-certified tempered — which means it is more likely to just crack or shatter into safe pieces – you still don't want to risk it cracking or exploding.
The other thing you need to check before you start installing your doors is that you are setting them up the right way. For this particular product, only one side slides. It's easy to flip it either way, but you have to set it up correctly to suit your needs, or you may be stuck trying to squeeze between your toilet and tub every time you need to shower.
There is also occasionally the issue of the shower door not fitting, despite the given measurements being perfect for your space. Some reviews mention that the details provided on the product page aren't exactly accurate. "Defective shower door. One side of the glass was too short and water was spilling out," said a 1-star review on Amazon .
It's not uncommon to buy an item when it goes on sale, or you have the money, and then open it to install it months later. However, It's a good idea to check that everything is included, and that the measurements are correct as soon as you get it. That way, you have time to return it through Amazon before the period ends. It's a bit of a pain, especially if you need to put it away again until you're ready to install, but it can save you a lot of frustration later.
Shower doors must fit your space very closely, so that you don't have to deal with gaps or leaks. Some reviewers mention measuring the length and width of all pieces several times, just to make sure everything will fit properly. You may also want to check the measurements in different spots, for both your door and the place you are installing it, as rooms aren't always even, either. What may seem like the right length in one spot may end up being too short in another.

articles.title_orig: 'The transit world is where innovation goes to die' — The U.S. lags far behind on using driverless trains, but new projects could open the floodgates
articles.title_zh: 'The transit world is where innovation goes to die' — The U.S. lags far behind on using driverless trains, but new projects could open the floodgates
articles.content_orig:
Even as automated vehicles such as robotaxis grow more prevalent in the U.S., almost every mass transit system still requires a driver or operator on board. Two major cities are seeking to change that.
Officials in Washington, D.C., recently advanced a plan that could let computers fully control one of its subways, and Los Angeles is seeking to build a new, completely automated line. Honolulu already has one.
The Washington and LA projects, which would take years to implement and still face financial and technical hurdles, come amid an already fierce debate over the safety risks and benefits of automated trains and whether the substantial upfront expense is worth the long-term savings in labor costs.
Supporters call the push long overdue, pointing out that American cities lag far behind numerous places across the world that run unattended subways, metros or buses, including several cities in Europe and Asia, as well as major systems in Canada, Australia, South America and the Middle East.
“It should be much harder to automate something that’s on-road, that has all of these various obstacles coming at it, compared to a fixed-rail system,” said Baruch Feigenbaum, senior managing director of transportation policy at the Reason Foundation, a libertarian think tank that has advocated for transit automation. “I don’t know a nice way to say this, but basically the transit world is where innovation goes to die.”
Only in recent years have on-road vehicles from such companies as Waymo, Tesla and Zoox taken the automation lead in the U.S. ahead of transit systems using a track. In fact, although operators have always been part of the Metro subway system in Washington, D.C., trains ran with some automated features when it opened 50 years ago. After a 2009 fatal crash, those were turned off, then restored over the past two years.
Now, officials in the nation’s capital have renewed their push for automation on Metro’s Red Line. And an environmental review is underway in Los Angeles for an automated track for a new underground line of its heavy-rail system that would cut through the rough terrain of the Santa Monica Mountains.
Honolulu is already running an elevated driverless line — the most expansive automated transit system in the U.S. It’ll stretch 19 miles when completed, surpassing the elevated driverless trains Detroit and Miami opened as pilot projects in the 1980s, a monorail connecting hotels on the Las Vegas Strip, and smaller systems that carry passengers between airport terminals.
An automated monorail that once ran in Memphis, Tennessee, closed down years ago. And the driverless Jacksonville Skyway will indefinitely halt operations soon due to budget cuts, despite initial plans for an even larger automated system.
After nine people were killed and many others injured in the 2009 train collision near the Fort Totten station on the D.C. Red Line, the National Transportation Safety Board blamed the crash on a maintenance problem in the automated signaling system that separates trains from one another.
Randy Clarke, CEO of the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority , pointed out in an interview with The Associated Press that the issue in Fort Totten had nothing to do with the cruise control-like system that was restored on the Red Line in 2024 and the other Metro lines last year. Still, he acknowledged that for many years the crash “paralyzed” Metro’s plans for further automation.
“That was a big failure, there’s no question. We do not do anything like that now,” said Clarke, who called the current system “highly regulated, highly documented, very proficient.”
Trains could conceivably run without a human worker inside the cab as early as 2033 under the nearly $1 billion plan Metro’s Board of Directors backed in April to upgrade the Red Line with safety features including protective barriers that prevent passengers from getting onto the tracks.
Clarke said that even if workers aren’t needed to physically run the trains, they will be needed to maintain the tracks and respond to emergencies.
Unions have been critics of automation. John Samuelsen, a former worker in the New York subway system who now serves as international president of the Transport Workers Union, said unions have fought off automation efforts in New York and elsewhere, calling them “a catastrophe waiting to happen.”
“Passengers will be left dealing with a self-evacuation, which is a disaster in a system which runs on a third rail,” Samuelsen said.
To alleviate massive traffic bottlenecks for commuters, Honolulu opened its Skyline automated light metro transit system three years ago and expanded it last year.
Vance Tsuda, the system’s project director, said there hasn’t been a single crash or injury associated with automation. Even hybrid systems are less safe than a completely automated one, he said, arguing that a human is far more likely to overlook something like an open door and prematurely clear a train for departure.
“If you have somebody making that decision, they could make a wrong decision,” Tsuda said.
But David King, an associate professor of urban planning at Arizona State University who has researched automated transportation, said the success rate has to remain perfect to keep the public trust. That’s why the Fort Totten crash and others involving automation put the technology so far behind, he said.
“We allow a certain amount of failure with private industry that we don’t tolerate when the state does it,” said King, citing the several rockets blown up by Elon Musk’s SpaceX — a record he argues would cripple NASA’s budget if it happened in the public sector.
Perhaps the most ambitious transit automation effort being pursued in the U.S. is the subway line Los Angeles officials voted to recommend beneath the Santa Monica Mountains. The area is one of the most notorious traffic headaches in the country, with the mountains dividing the bustling Westside employment hub from the San Fernando Valley.
There’s already a subway system under the same mountain range near Hollywood, but that one has a driver onboard. The new proposal, which is undergoing an environmental review, would use shorter, more frequent trains, said Cecily Way, who oversees planning for the Sepulveda Project for LA Metro.
Like the project in Washington, the new line in Los Angeles would feature station doors to protect passengers on the platform from oncoming trains.
Feigenbaum with the Reason Foundation said that automation of a major transit line such as in Los Angeles or Washington could open the floodgates for other cities to follow.
“It sends a signal that this is technologically doable and this is something that maybe other systems are going to want to strive for,” he said.

articles.title_orig: What to expect from Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ event
articles.title_zh: What to expect from Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ event
articles.content_orig:
Apple’s long-rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro, an OLED iPad Mini, and more.
Apple’s long-rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro, an OLED iPad Mini, and more.
It feels like Apple’s Welcome Home event just happened. And the iPhone Duo announcement isn’t all that far in our rearview mirror, either. Yet, the company is back with another launch, focused on the MacBook Pro, it looks like. Its “ Pro and tell ” event is scheduled for October 28th at 1PM ET in Los Angeles. While obviously nothing is confirmed yet, it sure seems like we’re finally going to get that long-rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro.
Beyond that? There could be an OLED update for the iPad Mini, plus M6 updates across other devices, following the M6 debut with the Mac Mini in August.
A MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen has been a fixture of the rumor mill since at least early 2023 . But now, in late 2026, it may finally come to fruition. The name MacBook Ultra has been floating around, but Apple is unlikely to rebrand its flagship laptop line.
This will be the first touchscreen laptop and the first OLED laptop from Apple. It will supposedly feature an iPhone-esque Dynamic Island, but don’t expect a dramatic revamp of the macOS interface — The touchscreen MacBook isn’t going to be some sort of iPad hybrid . It may include a few flourishes, like a magnification effect when you touch the screen or new gesture controls in native apps. But that’s it.
It’s also going to stick with the M5 series of chips for the time being — specifically, the M5 Pro and M5 Max. There might not be an M6 Pro or Max , even. Instead, Apple may wait to upgrade its higher-end processors until it introduces the M7 next year .
That doesn’t mean there won’t be an M6 MacBook Pro, however. The base model of the MacBook Pro could be getting a bump from the M5 after the M6 debuted in the Mac Mini earlier this year. It might also get a slight redesign, including a hole-punch style camera. Unfortunately, they’re also expected to come with a price increase as component shortages reverberate through the Apple lineup.
The iMac is also expected to get an M6 update, nearly two years after its last revision. Apple’s all-in-one desktop appears like it’s going to skip right over the M5. Don’t expect any real changes beyond that, though. But at least we might get some new color options, just like we did with the M4 model.
Another long-rumored device that might finally be making its debut on Wednesday is the OLED iPad Mini . Other than the iPad Pro, the tablet lineup has stuck with LCDs until now. The new OLED iPad could kick off a broader transition for the product line. The screen upgrade may add $100 to the cost, though. Otherwise, it likely won’t be a significant redesign, but expect a processor upgrade from the aging A17 to the A20 that debuted with the iPhone 18.
